history.summary: The Dattatreya Mahadeva Temple at Dattnagar is the shrine that gives the village its name: a 2024 research paper on the folk elements in the temple's sculptures states that 'Dattnagar village derives its name from the temple of Dattatreya' (zenodo.org paper, 'Folk Elements in the Sculptures of Dattatreya Mahadeva Temple at Dattnagar, Shimla District'). The temple stands on the left bank of the Sutlej on the main National Highway / Hindustan-Tibet Road near Rampur, and its holdings include sculptures of the main Hindu sects - Shaivite, Vaishnavite and Shakti; a life-size Vishnu sculpture found in a sand mine at Dattnagar points to ancient image worship in the region. Wikimapia also lists it as 'Duttatreya Swami mandir, Duttngar' among Rampur-area places of worship. TOWN CORRECTION: the CSV town 'Rampur' is approximate - the temple is at Dattnagar village near Rampur, so town has been corrected to Dattnagar. No founder, dynasty or built date is recorded in accessible sources. Coordinates are approximate Rampur-town coordinates (wikimapia: 31 deg 26'59"N 77 deg 37'47"E), since no POI-level position for the Dattnagar shrine was found.

name: Dattatreya Mahadeva Temple
town_description: Dattnagar is a village on the left bank of the Sutlej near Rampur in Shimla district, Himachal Pradesh, on the main Hindustan-Tibet highway (NH-5); it takes its name from its Dattatreya temple.
tradition: Hinduism (Dattatreya tradition; Shaivite and Vaishnavite elements)

travel.airport: Shimla Airport (Jubbarhatti), about 130 km from the Rampur area.
travel.railway: Nearest railhead: Shimla (narrow-gauge), about 130 km away; Kalka (broad gauge) is farther.
travel.road: Dattnagar lies on NH-5 (the old Hindustan-Tibet Road) near Rampur, about 130 km from Shimla; reachable by bus or taxi on the Shimla-Rampur route.

visitor_information.best_time: March to June and October to November.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not published online; daytime darshan typical of village temples.
